topic: How does the proposed tropical Z-R relationship impact Ka-band link margin calculations compared to the Marshall-Palmer model for satellite systems in high rainfall regions?
response: The proposed tropical Z-R relationship, with parameters (62, 1.6), predicts higher rainfall rates than the Marshall-Palmer model in high rainfall regions. This results in increased rain attenuation at Ka-band frequencies (e.g., 18.9 GHz). Consequently, link margin calculations for satellite systems in these regions must account for the more accurate tropical Z-R relationship to ensure reliable communication links.
reference_context: The reference context provides data on rain attenuation prediction models for satellite communications in tropical regions, including a proposed model with high accuracy in predicting cumulative distribution of rain attenuation. The analysis compares experimental results from nine tropical countries and identifies limitations in existing models.
